subject: [PATCH v2 0/5] btrfs: handle -ENOMEM errors in some synchronous dirops without aborting

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested simplifying the code by directly returning a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer, reducing the parameter list.
reviews.raw_body:
We can directly return a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer, which reduce 
the parameter list.

Otherwise looks good to me.

Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>

Thanks,
Qu

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo approved the patch, providing a Reviewed-by tag.

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that when a pre-allocated path is passed in and an earlier allocation fails, the function returns -ENOMEM without freeing the pre-allocated path, resulting in a memory leak.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested merging the memcpy operation into the preallocation function, citing that the preallocation itself doesn't utilize the name->name field.
reviews.raw_body:
This is exposed by sashiko.

If we have @prealloc passed in, and before we even hit 
insert_with_overflow(), the previous btrfs_alloc_path() failed, we 
return -ENOMEM directly, leaking the @prealloc.

---

Sashiko also pointed out that, the preallocation itself doesn't really 
utilize name->name.

Thus it may be a good idea to merge the later memcpy() into the 
preallocation function.

Thanks,
Qu

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to Qu Wenruo's feedback about allocating a btrfs_path on the stack in btrfs_insert_orphan_item(), stating that it is currently allocated by the caller and should remain so, but is open to being convinced otherwise.
reviews.raw_body:
...but then we'd have to allocate it separately. It's currently
allocated on the stack by the caller. I think we ought to keep it this
way, but I'm willing to be convinced otherwise.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that additional issues were missed in the original patchset and plans to address them in a new version (v3).
sentiment_signals: plans to spin up a v3
reviews.raw_body:
Good catch. It looks like sashiko also flagged some other similar
issues nearby too that we might as well fix while we're in here. I'll
plan to spin up a v3 and resend the series. Thanks very much for the
review so far!

-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a reviewer's point that checking for NULL pointer would be more natural, but expressed concern about adding another heap allocation in low-memory situations.
reviews.raw_body:
It's a good point. It is more natural to be able to just look and say
"NULL pointer means no prealloc".

OTOH, the entire reason we're doing this is to deal with low-memory
situations. Do we want to add another heap allocation into this
codepath?

Either way, I'll think about it.

Thanks again for the review!
--
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

2026-08-05.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a long-standing issue in the Btrfs file system where memory allocation failures can cause the file system to abort. The patches rework the code to perform memory allocations before critical points, preventing aborts due to ENOMEM errors. This includes changes to directory morphing and orphan handling, with additional tests added to exercise the new behavior. While not all potential cases are covered, this series is designed to work in conjunction with other patches to address remaining issues.

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that only two callsites use on-stack memory for the prealloc structure and suggested converting to a heap-based solution. Additionally, they pointed out a potential issue with the lifespan management of btrfs_dir_index_prealloc, suggesting a more straightforward approach using regular heap memory allocation.
